issues.description: NamespaceSealed stub returns false unconditionally while security-sensitive callers already depend on it
issues.detail: Core.NamespaceSealed always returns false with a TODO, yet ListAllNamespaces, loadLoginMFAConfigs, countActiveTokens, and metrics paths are wired against it. A stub that lies is worse than no stub: every caller now encodes a falsehood as fact. Either land SealManager in the same patch, gate callers behind a build tag, or return an explicit error that fails closed.

issues.description: ACL root contract silently widened to ancestor check via HasParent without stated invariant or spec
issues.detail: ACL.root changed from bool to *namespace.Namespace; AllowOperation now grants root via ns.HasParent(a.root). HasParent's reflexivity and ancestry semantics are unstated, and the new contract (root in N grants root across descendants) is undocumented. This is a security-critical LSP-style broadening of the trust boundary with no written invariant or proof.

issues.description: ErrNamespaceSealed dispatch uses substring matching on error text instead of errors.Is on the sentinel
issues.detail: AdjustErrorStatusCode calls errwrap.Contains(err, consts.ErrNamespaceSealed.Error()), a substring search on 'namespace is sealed'. Any wrapped error whose text happens to contain that phrase is silently coerced to 503. Treat errors as values: use errors.Is on the sentinel so wrapping and translation work correctly.

issues.description: ACL test coverage for new ancestry semantics is thin; missing sibling, cousin, deep-descendant, and self cases
issues.detail: testACLRoot only exercises self-ns allow and root-context deny, with an ad-hoc namespace literal lacking an ID. The new HasParent gate is the authorization boundary and needs an exhaustive matrix: reflexive self, direct child, deep descendant, sibling denial, cousin denial, and root-of-root behavior. Without this, a latent privilege-escalation path can ship undetected.

issues.description: AllowOperation silently returns empty deny on namespace.FromContext error with no diagnostic
issues.detail: The reordered ns lookup at the top of AllowOperation returns an empty ACLResults on error before any log or audit, indistinguishable from a normal deny. Previously root fast-path did not require ns; now a missing namespace silently denies every root operation. At minimum log and distinguish 'no namespace' from 'denied', or preserve the prior root behavior with a stated precondition.

issues.description: NSTokenLength formula uses opaque "."[1] byte-indexing instead of a named separator constant
issues.detail: Computing length via TokenLen + "."[1] + nsID indexes a one-byte string literal to obtain a separator length. It is gratuitously clever and fragile to separator changes. Name a const NSTokenSeparator = '.' (or use len(".")) and write the arithmetic plainly so intent survives the next reader.

synthesis.summary: The panel converges on a security-critical verdict: the PR widens the ACL root-policy contract from 'root namespace only' to 'any namespace with descendant ancestry via HasParent' without stating the new invariant, and ships a NamespaceSealed stub that unconditionally returns false while live security-sensitive callers already depend on it. The sealed-error status mapping uses substring matching on error text where errors.Is on the sentinel is the correct structured form. Test coverage for the new ancestry semantics is thin (only self and root-context cases) and does not exercise sibling, cousin, or deep-descendant scenarios. Smaller issues include silent empty-deny on FromContext error in AllowOperation and the opaque \".\"[1] arithmetic in NSTokenLength. Recommend splitting the ACL change out as its own patch, documenting the new invariants, fixing the stub to fail closed or land with SealManager, and switching to errors.Is before merge.
